rich_narrative.summary: The Islamic Association of Arabi, operating as Masjid Yaseen, is a long-standing religious and educational institution that has served its community since <cite id="1">its founding in 1985</cite>. The organization manages several specialized educational programs, including the <cite id="2">Al-Hameed Boys Academy and the Amatur Rahman Girls Academy</cite>, alongside a Hifz and Alim school. While the charity maintains a <cite id="3">high program expense ratio of 96.2%</cite> according to recent financial filings, it faces significant structural challenges that limit its overall effectiveness. Most notably, the organization operates with <cite id="4">a board of only one member</cite>, which presents a severe governance risk and lacks the oversight typically expected of a multi-million dollar nonprofit. Financially, the charity reported <cite id="5">total revenue of $2,357,167 in FY2023</cite>, yet it holds <cite id="6">38.8 months of working capital</cite> in reserve. This level of accumulation is considered excessive for a charity that <cite id="7">collects zakat for the needy</cite>, as Islamic tradition and nonprofit best practices generally favor the prompt distribution of funds to those in need rather than long-term hoarding of liquid assets.
